Can someone from sales/solutions help with a short call to confirm fit and next steps?

Karthik — thanks for the quick reply. Answers inline below.

- Typical request: 80 tokens input / 64 tokens completion average.
- Bursts: usually 10–20 minute bursts during business hours, up to the 300 concurrent requests noted. Sustained baseline is ~40 qps.
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 250ms, p99 < 600ms for short generations.
- Region: prefer us-west for lower RTT.

Tue/Wed mornings PT work. Can you book Tue 11:30 PT? Also, we'd like a short rundown on: autoscaling burst handling, KV cache options for repeated prefixes, and how fallbacks to hosted models would behave if Dedicated capacity is saturated.

—Samantha

Thanks Samantha — I've blocked Tue 11:30 PT for a 30-min intro and added a 45-min follow-up slot at Tue 12:15 PT in case we need the deeper technical run. Invites attached (calendar-invite.ics).

Agenda (30-min intro):
- Quick AtlasData goals & traffic profile (5 min)
- Redwood Dedicated overview + burst/autoscale behavior (10 min)
- Q&A and next steps (15 min)

If the team is technical, we'll use the follow-up slot to review: model selection, quantization options (int8/4), KV cache placement, and an estimated throughput plan for your burst profile.

A few notes up-front:
- Based on 80/64 tokens and 300 concurrent bursts, we likely recommend a Dedicated pool with autoscale headroom for ~500 concurrent soft capacity to avoid throttling during peak windows — we'll model this live.
- Fallbacks: policy-based routing can send overflow to a compatible hosted variant; this is opt-in and logged for audit.

Attaching a draft MAP (mutual action plan) and our quicksheet to help prepare.
